旧[[県社]]|創建=不詳|本殿=|別名=岡の宮|札所等=|例祭=[[10月17日]]|神事=}} [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_torii.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|Torii}}]] '''Sasutahiko Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in Kataoka-cho, [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]] [[Wakayama Prefecture|City, Wakayama Prefecture]] . It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. The only known document that mentions "Sashidahiko" is the "Furuya Family Genealogy" included in the "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Shiho" 『甲斐国一之宮浅間神社誌』浅間神社、1979年、資料篇のpp. 278-300所収。古屋家は[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]の社家。 . The "Furuya Family Genealogy" states that Michiomi’s father was Sasadahiko, and that Michiomi was “born in Kataoka, Nagusa County, Kii Province.” [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 Based on this record, the Sasadahiko Shrine has speculated that Sasadahiko was originally enshrined as an ancestral deity. The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] . In addition, the Kii no [[:ja:紀伊国神名帳|Kuni Jinmyo-]] cho records him as "Sashidahiko-no-Kami, Junior Fourth Rank Upper (or Junior Fifth Rank Upper)." Mitsuyo was a swordsmith from Miike, Chikugo Province, in the late Kamakura period. The mounting is a thread-wrapped tachi mounting, with all metal fittings made of red copper with a gold-colored diamond pattern on a fish roe background, the scabbard with a gold-colored diamond pattern lacquer-e on a gold pear-colored background, and the handle and waving are brown with a gold border and flower-colored thread winding. The sword box was painted black with wax, had a hinged lid and a lock. 文化庁編『戦災等による焼失文化財 増訂版 美術工芸篇』（臨川書店、1983年）。 In [[Taishō period|1924]] [[1924|,]] it was designated as a former national treasure (equivalent to [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|an important cultural property]] under current law) based on the Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Law of the [[Shōwa period|time]], but was destroyed by fire during the Great Wakayama Air Raid on July 9, [[1945]] . == Festivals == '''location''' * 2-9 Kataokacho [[Wakayama (city)|, Wakayama City,]] Wakayama [[Wakayama Prefecture|Prefecture]] '''Traffic access''' * From Wakayama Station on the West Japan Railway Company (JR West Japan) or Wakayamashi Station on the JR West Japan/ Nankai Electric Railway Company ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Okayamacho" bus stop (approximately 5 minutes walk from the bus stop) ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Kencho-mae" bus stop (approximately 7 minutes walk from the bus stop) == Local information == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == footnote == * Shrine History Book * Shikinaisha Research Group (ed.), Shikinaisha Research Report, Kokugakuin University Press, 1977-86 * Junichi Kamada (ed.), "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Jisho," Sengen Jinja, March 10, 1979 * Nozaki Sabun, "Japanese Scenic Places and Geographies, Volume 8: Nankaido Section," Hakubunkan, 1898 * Yoshiyasu Shimizu, Catalog of Famous Places in Japan, Wakayama Prefecture Volume, Taiseikan, 1904 * Edited and published by Wakayama City Hall, "Wakayama History Supplement Edition," Wakayama City Hall, 1915 * " Japanese Historical Place names : Place names in Wakayama Prefecture" ( Heibonsha ) - {{Draft}}{{complex}}{{infobox religious building|名称=刺田比古神社| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Sasutahiko-jinja haiden-01.JPG|280px]]|caption=[[Haiden]]|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{coordinates|34|13|25.66|N|135|10|26.77|E}}|location=[[Wakayama Prefecture]] [[Wakayama City]] Kataoka-cho 2-9|deity={{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}}
{{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}}
{{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}}|位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|13|25.66|N|135|10|26.77|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=刺田比古神社}}|祭神=[[道臣命]]
[[大伴狭手彦|大伴佐氐比古命]]|神体=|社格=[[式内社]]（小）
旧[[県社]]|創建=不詳|本殿=|別名=岡の宮|札所等=|例祭=[[10月17日]]|神事=}} [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_torii.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|Torii}}]] '''Sasutahiko Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in Kataoka-cho, [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]] [[Wakayama Prefecture|City, Wakayama Prefecture]] . It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. The only known document that mentions "Sashidahiko" is the "Furuya Family Genealogy" included in the "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Shiho" 『甲斐国一之宮浅間神社誌』浅間神社、1979年、資料篇のpp. 278-300所収。古屋家は[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]の社家。 . The "Furuya Family Genealogy" states that Michiomi’s father was Sasadahiko, and that Michiomi was “born in Kataoka, Nagusa County, Kii Province.” [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 Based on this record, the Sasadahiko Shrine has speculated that Sasadahiko was originally enshrined as an ancestral deity. The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] . In addition, the Kii no [[:ja:紀伊国神名帳|Kuni Jinmyo-]] cho records him as "Sashidahiko-no-Kami, Junior Fourth Rank Upper (or Junior Fifth Rank Upper)." During [[Edo period|the Edo period]], [[:ja:徳川頼宣|Tokugawa Yorinobu]] restored the shrine as a guardian deity for Wakayama Castle. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In addition, [[Tokugawa Yoshimune]] revered Sasadahiko Shrine as the local guardian deity and donated 10 koku of land to the [[1712|shrine]] in [[Shōtoku (era)|1712.]] 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[1594]], the [[Bunroku|temple]] grounds were moved to its current location 神社由緒書。, and in [[Genroku|1699]], [[:ja:吉田兼敬|Urabe Kaneyoshi]] designated it as a shrine listed in the Engishiki (Engishiki [[1699|Period]] ) under the name Sasadahiko Shrine 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 . Much of the origins of the shrine remain unclear due to the destruction of ancient documents and other materials through fire. According to the shrine's legend, when Okamoto Takehide, the 28th generation descendant of Otomo no Takemochi, first built Okayama Castle (present-day Wakayama City), he donated the shrine's land and revered it as the castle's guardian deity. 神社由緒書。 After that, the area fell into disrepair due to conflicts during [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]] . According to the Kii Shodo Fudoki, the shrine was revived by [[1443|parishioners]] during the [[Kakitsu]] era ( [[1441|1441-1443]] ). In [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|1585]] [[1585|,]] the shrine's land was confiscated when the Hashiba clan entered the country, but the [[:ja:和歌山城|Wakayama Castle]] lord, [[:ja:桑山重晴|Kuwayama Shigeharu]], restored the shrine buildings. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] considered Sasadahiko Shrine to be important as the guardian deity when he built Wakayama Castle. 神社由緒書。 In 1729, 200 koku of land from Tajiri Village in Nagusa County was donated to [[Kyōhō|him]] . 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 508。 It is also said to be a shrine where people pray for the peace of the nation, and is ordered to perform purification rituals for the peace of the nation 10,000 times a year. 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 247。 From [[Kan'ei|1626]] [[Kanbun (era)|to]] [[1626|1673]] [[1673|,]] Shoshuin served as the temple's betto temple. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, in April [[1873]], it was ranked as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]] under [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system]] . 神社由緒書。 Subsequently, the shrine buildings, treasures, and ancient records were destroyed in fire during the Pacific War. === God Tier === * Junior Fourth Rank Upper ( Kiino Jinmyocho ) - Written as "Sashidahiko-no-kami". Some manuscripts state that he was of Junior Fifth Rank Upper. === Priest === When Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Wakayama Castle, he appointed Okamoto Sasuke, a descendant of the Otomo clan, as its chief priest. 神社由緒書。 In addition, during the restoration by Shigeharu Kuwayama, Iechika Okamoto was designated a priest. Since then, generations of the Okamoto family have served as priests at Sasadahiko Shrine, Okamoto Chojun served as a temporary guardian for Tokugawa Yoshimune, and after Okamoto Chokoku, each generation has had an audience with the shogun once every three years, down to the present day. 神社由緒書。 == Temple grounds == === Shrine === The temple grounds were burned down during the war in 1945, but were later rebuilt. The [[1811]] " [[Bunka|Kiino]] Kuni Meisho Zue" lists Sasadahiko Shrine at the top of its list of famous places, and includes a drawing of the shrine grounds as they were at the time. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|alt=本殿|Main Hall File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|alt=拝殿|Worship hall === Okanosato Tomb === The ancient tomb is located on the slope of the mountain on the southwest side of the temple grounds and was discovered in January [[1932]] 境内説明板。 . Based on the shape of the pottery excavated, it is estimated to date to around [[6th century|the 6th century]] 『和歌山県史蹟名勝天然記念物調査報告 11輯』（和歌山県、1933年）。, and connections to Sasadahiko Shrine and the Otomo clan have been pointed out . The burial mound is currently buried under falling sand. Only one burial mound has been discovered, but if it is in the form of a group of burial mounds there is a possibility that there are more undiscovered burial mounds. {{Draft}}{{complex}}{{infobox religious building|名称=刺田比古神社| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Sasutahiko-jinja haiden-01.JPG|280px]]|caption=[[Haiden]]|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{coordinates|34|13|25.66|N|135|10|26.77|E}}|location=[[Wakayama Prefecture]] [[Wakayama City]] Kataoka-cho 2-9|deity={{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}}
{{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}}
{{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}}|位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|13|25.66|N|135|10|26.77|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=刺田比古神社}}|祭神=[[道臣命]]
[[大伴狭手彦|大伴佐氐比古命]]|神体=|社格=[[式内社]]（小）
旧[[県社]]|創建=不詳|本殿=|別名=岡の宮|札所等=|例祭=[[10月17日]]|神事=}} [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_torii.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|Torii}}]] '''Sasutahiko Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in Kataoka-cho, [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]] [[Wakayama Prefecture|City, Wakayama Prefecture]] . It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. The only known document that mentions "Sashidahiko" is the "Furuya Family Genealogy" included in the "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Shiho" 『甲斐国一之宮浅間神社誌』浅間神社、1979年、資料篇のpp. 278-300所収。古屋家は[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]の社家。 . The "Furuya Family Genealogy" states that Michiomi’s father was Sasadahiko, and that Michiomi was “born in Kataoka, Nagusa County, Kii Province.” [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 Based on this record, the Sasadahiko Shrine has speculated that Sasadahiko was originally enshrined as an ancestral deity. The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] . In addition, the Kii no [[:ja:紀伊国神名帳|Kuni Jinmyo-]] cho records him as "Sashidahiko-no-Kami, Junior Fourth Rank Upper (or Junior Fifth Rank Upper)." During [[Edo period|the Edo period]], [[:ja:徳川頼宣|Tokugawa Yorinobu]] restored the shrine as a guardian deity for Wakayama Castle. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In addition, [[Tokugawa Yoshimune]] revered Sasadahiko Shrine as the local guardian deity and donated 10 koku of land to the [[1712|shrine]] in [[Shōtoku (era)|1712.]] 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[1594]], the [[Bunroku|temple]] grounds were moved to its current location 神社由緒書。, and in [[Genroku|1699]], [[:ja:吉田兼敬|Urabe Kaneyoshi]] designated it as a shrine listed in the Engishiki (Engishiki [[1699|Period]] ) under the name Sasadahiko Shrine 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 . Much of the origins of the shrine remain unclear due to the destruction of ancient documents and other materials through fire. According to the shrine's legend, when Okamoto Takehide, the 28th generation descendant of Otomo no Takemochi, first built Okayama Castle (present-day Wakayama City), he donated the shrine's land and revered it as the castle's guardian deity. 神社由緒書。 After that, the area fell into disrepair due to conflicts during [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]] . According to the Kii Shodo Fudoki, the shrine was revived by [[1443|parishioners]] during the [[Kakitsu]] era ( [[1441|1441-1443]] ). In [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|1585]] [[1585|,]] the shrine's land was confiscated when the Hashiba clan entered the country, but the [[:ja:和歌山城|Wakayama Castle]] lord, [[:ja:桑山重晴|Kuwayama Shigeharu]], restored the shrine buildings. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] considered Sasadahiko Shrine to be important as the guardian deity when he built Wakayama Castle. 神社由緒書。 In 1729, 200 koku of land from Tajiri Village in Nagusa County was donated to [[Kyōhō|him]] . 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 508。 It is also said to be a shrine where people pray for the peace of the nation, and is ordered to perform purification rituals for the peace of the nation 10,000 times a year. 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 247。 From [[Kan'ei|1626]] [[Kanbun (era)|to]] [[1626|1673]] [[1673|,]] Shoshuin served as the temple's betto temple. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, in April [[1873]], it was ranked as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]] under [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system]] . 神社由緒書。 Subsequently, the shrine buildings, treasures, and ancient records were destroyed in fire during the Pacific War. === God Tier === * Junior Fourth Rank Upper ( Kiino Jinmyocho ) - Written as "Sashidahiko-no-kami". Some manuscripts state that he was of Junior Fifth Rank Upper. === Priest === When Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Wakayama Castle, he appointed Okamoto Sasuke, a descendant of the Otomo clan, as its chief priest. 神社由緒書。 In addition, during the restoration by Shigeharu Kuwayama, Iechika Okamoto was designated a priest. Since then, generations of the Okamoto family have served as priests at Sasadahiko Shrine, Okamoto Chojun served as a temporary guardian for Tokugawa Yoshimune, and after Okamoto Chokoku, each generation has had an audience with the shogun once every three years, down to the present day. 神社由緒書。 == Temple grounds == === Shrine === The temple grounds were burned down during the war in 1945, but were later rebuilt. The [[1811]] " [[Bunka|Kiino]] Kuni Meisho Zue" lists Sasadahiko Shrine at the top of its list of famous places, and includes a drawing of the shrine grounds as they were at the time. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|alt=本殿|Main Hall File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|alt=拝殿|Worship hall === Okanosato Tomb === The ancient tomb is located on the slope of the mountain on the southwest side of the temple grounds and was discovered in January [[1932]] 境内説明板。 . Based on the shape of the pottery excavated, it is estimated to date to around [[6th century|the 6th century]] 『和歌山県史蹟名勝天然記念物調査報告 11輯』（和歌山県、1933年）。, and connections to Sasadahiko Shrine and the Otomo clan have been pointed out . The burial mound is currently buried under falling sand. Only one burial mound has been discovered, but if it is in the form of a group of burial mounds there is a possibility that there are more undiscovered burial mounds. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|alt=岡の里古墳の位置|location of Okanosato Tomb == Sub-shrines == === Affiliated shrines === [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_Hachiman-sha_&_Hikawa-sha.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|八幡社・氷川社}}]] * Hachiman Shrine - deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]] 摂末社の記載は神社由緒書による。 * Hikawa Shrine - deity: [[Susanoo]] === Sub-shrine === * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Konpira Shrine - deity: Omononushi * Usumisha Shrine - deity: Usumi * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Kobayashi Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama no Mikoto * Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime * Kasuga Shrine - Deities: Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto, Inahinushi-no-Mikoto, Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto, Himegami * Tenmangu Shrine - deity: Sugawara no Michizane * Haraedo Shrine - Deities: Seoritsuhime, Hayaakitsuhime, Ibukito no Kami, Hayasasurahime * Nanryu Hattattsusha Shrine - deity: Nanryu Hattattsu Okami * Daikokusha - deity: Okuninushi * Divine Horse - deity: Lord Aritoku (Tokugawa Yoshimune)'s beloved horse * == deity ==

== Cultural Assets == === Cultural properties destroyed by fire === * Sword with the name Mitsuyo *: [[Tachi|This sword]] is said to have been donated by [[Kyōhō|Tokugawa]] [[Tokugawa Yoshimune|Yoshimune]] in [[1721]] . Mitsuyo was a swordsmith from Miike, Chikugo Province, in the late Kamakura period. The mounting is a thread-wrapped tachi mounting, with all metal fittings made of red copper with a gold-colored diamond pattern on a fish roe background, the scabbard with a gold-colored diamond pattern lacquer-e on a gold pear-colored background, and the handle and waving are brown with a gold border and flower-colored thread winding. The sword box was painted black with wax, had a hinged lid and a lock. 文化庁編『戦災等による焼失文化財 増訂版 美術工芸篇』（臨川書店、1983年）。 In [[Taishō period|1924]] [[1924|,]] it was designated as a former national treasure (equivalent to [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|an important cultural property]] under current law) based on the Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Law of the [[Shōwa period|time]], but was destroyed by fire during the Great Wakayama Air Raid on July 9, [[1945]] . == Festivals == '''location''' * 2-9 Kataokacho [[Wakayama (city)|, Wakayama City,]] Wakayama [[Wakayama Prefecture|Prefecture]] '''Traffic access''' * From Wakayama Station on the West Japan Railway Company (JR West Japan) or Wakayamashi Station on the JR West Japan/ Nankai Electric Railway Company ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Okayamacho" bus stop (approximately 5 minutes walk from the bus stop) ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Kencho-mae" bus stop (approximately 7 minutes walk from the bus stop) == Local information == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == footnote == * Shrine History Book * Shikinaisha Research Group (ed.), Shikinaisha Research Report, Kokugakuin University Press, 1977-86 * Junichi Kamada (ed.), "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Jisho," Sengen Jinja, March 10, 1979 * Nozaki Sabun, "Japanese Scenic Places and Geographies, Volume 8: Nankaido Section," Hakubunkan, 1898 * Yoshiyasu Shimizu, Catalog of Famous Places in Japan, Wakayama Prefecture Volume, Taiseikan, 1904 * Edited and published by Wakayama City Hall, "Wakayama History Supplement Edition," Wakayama City Hall, 1915 * " Japanese Historical Place names : Place names in Wakayama Prefecture" ( Heibonsha ) - According to the Kojiki, he served as the vanguard during {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}} . * {{ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} *: In the "Nihon Shoki" he is written as "Sadehiko." 旧[[県社]]|創建=不詳|本殿=|別名=岡の宮|札所等=|例祭=[[10月17日]]|神事=}} [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_torii.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|Torii}}]] '''Sasutahiko Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in Kataoka-cho, [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]] [[Wakayama Prefecture|City, Wakayama Prefecture]] . It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. The only known document that mentions "Sashidahiko" is the "Furuya Family Genealogy" included in the "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Shiho" 『甲斐国一之宮浅間神社誌』浅間神社、1979年、資料篇のpp. 278-300所収。古屋家は[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]の社家。 . The "Furuya Family Genealogy" states that Michiomi’s father was Sasadahiko, and that Michiomi was “born in Kataoka, Nagusa County, Kii Province.” [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 Based on this record, the Sasadahiko Shrine has speculated that Sasadahiko was originally enshrined as an ancestral deity. The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] . In addition, the Kii no [[:ja:紀伊国神名帳|Kuni Jinmyo-]] cho records him as "Sashidahiko-no-Kami, Junior Fourth Rank Upper (or Junior Fifth Rank Upper)." During [[Edo period|the Edo period]], [[:ja:徳川頼宣|Tokugawa Yorinobu]] restored the shrine as a guardian deity for Wakayama Castle. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In addition, [[Tokugawa Yoshimune]] revered Sasadahiko Shrine as the local guardian deity and donated 10 koku of land to the [[1712|shrine]] in [[Shōtoku (era)|1712.]] 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[1594]], the [[Bunroku|temple]] grounds were moved to its current location 神社由緒書。, and in [[Genroku|1699]], [[:ja:吉田兼敬|Urabe Kaneyoshi]] designated it as a shrine listed in the Engishiki (Engishiki [[1699|Period]] ) under the name Sasadahiko Shrine 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 . Much of the origins of the shrine remain unclear due to the destruction of ancient documents and other materials through fire. According to the shrine's legend, when Okamoto Takehide, the 28th generation descendant of Otomo no Takemochi, first built Okayama Castle (present-day Wakayama City), he donated the shrine's land and revered it as the castle's guardian deity. 神社由緒書。 After that, the area fell into disrepair due to conflicts during [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]] . According to the Kii Shodo Fudoki, the shrine was revived by [[1443|parishioners]] during the [[Kakitsu]] era ( [[1441|1441-1443]] ). In [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|1585]] [[1585|,]] the shrine's land was confiscated when the Hashiba clan entered the country, but the [[:ja:和歌山城|Wakayama Castle]] lord, [[:ja:桑山重晴|Kuwayama Shigeharu]], restored the shrine buildings. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] considered Sasadahiko Shrine to be important as the guardian deity when he built Wakayama Castle. 神社由緒書。 In 1729, 200 koku of land from Tajiri Village in Nagusa County was donated to [[Kyōhō|him]] . 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 508。 It is also said to be a shrine where people pray for the peace of the nation, and is ordered to perform purification rituals for the peace of the nation 10,000 times a year. 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 247。 From [[Kan'ei|1626]] [[Kanbun (era)|to]] [[1626|1673]] [[1673|,]] Shoshuin served as the temple's betto temple. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, in April [[1873]], it was ranked as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]] under [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system]] . 神社由緒書。 Subsequently, the shrine buildings, treasures, and ancient records were destroyed in fire during the Pacific War. === God Tier === * Junior Fourth Rank Upper ( Kiino Jinmyocho ) - Written as "Sashidahiko-no-kami". Some manuscripts state that he was of Junior Fifth Rank Upper. === Priest === When Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Wakayama Castle, he appointed Okamoto Sasuke, a descendant of the Otomo clan, as its chief priest. 神社由緒書。 In addition, during the restoration by Shigeharu Kuwayama, Iechika Okamoto was designated a priest. Since then, generations of the Okamoto family have served as priests at Sasadahiko Shrine, Okamoto Chojun served as a temporary guardian for Tokugawa Yoshimune, and after Okamoto Chokoku, each generation has had an audience with the shogun once every three years, down to the present day. 神社由緒書。 == Temple grounds == === Shrine === The temple grounds were burned down during the war in 1945, but were later rebuilt. The [[1811]] " [[Bunka|Kiino]] Kuni Meisho Zue" lists Sasadahiko Shrine at the top of its list of famous places, and includes a drawing of the shrine grounds as they were at the time. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|alt=本殿|Main Hall File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|alt=拝殿|Worship hall === Okanosato Tomb === The ancient tomb is located on the slope of the mountain on the southwest side of the temple grounds and was discovered in January [[1932]] 境内説明板。 . Based on the shape of the pottery excavated, it is estimated to date to around [[6th century|the 6th century]] 『和歌山県史蹟名勝天然記念物調査報告 11輯』（和歌山県、1933年）。, and connections to Sasadahiko Shrine and the Otomo clan have been pointed out . The burial mound is currently buried under falling sand. Only one burial mound has been discovered, but if it is in the form of a group of burial mounds there is a possibility that there are more undiscovered burial mounds. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|alt=岡の里古墳の位置|location of Okanosato Tomb == Sub-shrines == === Affiliated shrines === [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_Hachiman-sha_&_Hikawa-sha.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|八幡社・氷川社}}]] * Hachiman Shrine - deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]] 摂末社の記載は神社由緒書による。 * Hikawa Shrine - deity: [[Susanoo]] === Sub-shrine === * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Konpira Shrine - deity: Omononushi * Usumisha Shrine - deity: Usumi * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Kobayashi Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama no Mikoto * Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime * Kasuga Shrine - Deities: Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto, Inahinushi-no-Mikoto, Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto, Himegami * Tenmangu Shrine - deity: Sugawara no Michizane * Haraedo Shrine - Deities: Seoritsuhime, Hayaakitsuhime, Ibukito no Kami, Hayasasurahime * Nanryu Hattattsusha Shrine - deity: Nanryu Hattattsu Okami * Daikokusha - deity: Okuninushi * Divine Horse - deity: Lord Aritoku (Tokugawa Yoshimune)'s beloved horse * == deity ==
festival List
* monthly ** Tsukikami Festival (1st) - Small festival 祭事の記載は神社由緒書による。 . ** Monthly Festival (17th) - Small festival. * January ** New Year's Day Festival, Ceremony to pray for the safety of parishioners (January 1st) - both are medium-sized festivals. ** Genshisai (January 3rd) - Middle festival. ** Coming of Age Festival (January: Coming of Age Day) - A small festival. * February ** Setsubun Festival (Setsubun Day in February) - A small festival. ** Kigensetsu Festival (February 11th) - A small festival. ** Hatsuuma Festival (Hatsuuma Day on the lunar calendar in February) - A small festival. * March ** '''Prayer Festival''' (Spring Festival) (March 17th) - '''Grand festival''' . ** Goryo-sai (March, Vernal Equinox Day) - A small festival. * April ** Greenery Day Festival (April 29th) - Medium festival. * May ** Constitution Memorial Festival (May 3rd) - Small festival. ** Benten Festival (May 5th) - Small festival. * July ** Summer Festival (July 17th) - Mid-year festival. * September ** Goryo-sai (Autumnal Equinox Day, September) - A small festival. * October ** '''festival''' (Autumn festival), '''Kanname-sai''' (October 17th) - both '''are major festivals''' . * November ** Culture Festival (November 3rd) - Mid-year festival. ** '''Niiname-sai''' (Thanksgiving) (November 23rd) -Great '''festival''' . * December ** Fire Festival (Winter Festival) (December 13th) - Medium festival. ** Emperor's Birthday Festival (December 23rd) - Medium festival. ** Great Purification Ceremony (December 30th) - A small festival.
== Cultural Assets == === Cultural properties destroyed by fire === * Sword with the name Mitsuyo *: [[Tachi|This sword]] is said to have been donated by [[Kyōhō|Tokugawa]] [[Tokugawa Yoshimune|Yoshimune]] in [[1721]] . Mitsuyo was a swordsmith from Miike, Chikugo Province, in the late Kamakura period. The mounting is a thread-wrapped tachi mounting, with all metal fittings made of red copper with a gold-colored diamond pattern on a fish roe background, the scabbard with a gold-colored diamond pattern lacquer-e on a gold pear-colored background, and the handle and waving are brown with a gold border and flower-colored thread winding. The sword box was painted black with wax, had a hinged lid and a lock. 文化庁編『戦災等による焼失文化財 増訂版 美術工芸篇』（臨川書店、1983年）。 In [[Taishō period|1924]] [[1924|,]] it was designated as a former national treasure (equivalent to [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|an important cultural property]] under current law) based on the Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Law of the [[Shōwa period|time]], but was destroyed by fire during the Great Wakayama Air Raid on July 9, [[1945]] . == Festivals == '''location''' * 2-9 Kataokacho [[Wakayama (city)|, Wakayama City,]] Wakayama [[Wakayama Prefecture|Prefecture]] '''Traffic access''' * From Wakayama Station on the West Japan Railway Company (JR West Japan) or Wakayamashi Station on the JR West Japan/ Nankai Electric Railway Company ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Okayamacho" bus stop (approximately 5 minutes walk from the bus stop) ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Kencho-mae" bus stop (approximately 7 minutes walk from the bus stop) == Local information == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == footnote == * Shrine History Book * Shikinaisha Research Group (ed.), Shikinaisha Research Report, Kokugakuin University Press, 1977-86 * Junichi Kamada (ed.), "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Jisho," Sengen Jinja, March 10, 1979 * Nozaki Sabun, "Japanese Scenic Places and Geographies, Volume 8: Nankaido Section," Hakubunkan, 1898 * Yoshiyasu Shimizu, Catalog of Famous Places in Japan, Wakayama Prefecture Volume, Taiseikan, 1904 * Edited and published by Wakayama City Hall, "Wakayama History Supplement Edition," Wakayama City Hall, 1915 * " Japanese Historical Place names : Place names in Wakayama Prefecture" ( Heibonsha ) - Wakayama City, Sasadahiko Shrine * Maruyama Kentoku, "Sashidahiko Shrine" (in Kenichi Tanigawa ed., "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 6, Ise, Shima, Iga, Kii" ( Hakusuisha )) * Takao Takaga, "The Otomo Clan: A Famous Warrior Family Descended from the Native Peoples of the Japanese Archipelago (Research on Ancient Clans)," Aogaki Publishing, 2013 * {{ill|Michinoomi-no-mikoto|10=ja|11=道臣命}} *: Ancestor of the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|lt=Ōtomo clan|en}}. According to the Kojiki, he served as the vanguard during {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}} . * {{ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} *: In the "Nihon Shoki" he is written as "Sadehiko." He was the son of {{ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}}, and according to the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}, was the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto. He was sent to the Korean Peninsula and is said to have achieved military success. == External link == {{draft categories| [[Category:coordinates on Wikidata]] [[Category:Pages with unreviewed translations]] [[fr:User:{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Sasihiko Shrine]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Sasadahiko Shrine]] [[Category:File]] [[Category:refreshing the redirects]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Sasadahiko Shrine]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Sasihiko Shrine]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[en:draft: Sasadahiko Shrine]] }}

The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] . In addition, the Kii no [[:ja:紀伊国神名帳|Kuni Jinmyo-]] cho records him as "Sashidahiko-no-Kami, Junior Fourth Rank Upper (or Junior Fifth Rank Upper)." During [[Edo period|the Edo period]], [[:ja:徳川頼宣|Tokugawa Yorinobu]] restored the shrine as a guardian deity for Wakayama Castle. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In addition, [[Tokugawa Yoshimune]] revered Sasadahiko Shrine as the local guardian deity and donated 10 koku of land to the [[1712|shrine]] in [[Shōtoku (era)|1712.]] 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[1594]], the [[Bunroku|temple]] grounds were moved to its current location 神社由緒書。, and in [[Genroku|1699]], [[:ja:吉田兼敬|Urabe Kaneyoshi]] designated it as a shrine listed in the Engishiki (Engishiki [[1699|Period]] ) under the name Sasadahiko Shrine 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 . Much of the origins of the shrine remain unclear due to the destruction of ancient documents and other materials through fire. According to the shrine's legend, when Okamoto Takehide, the 28th generation descendant of Otomo no Takemochi, first built Okayama Castle (present-day Wakayama City), he donated the shrine's land and revered it as the castle's guardian deity. 神社由緒書。 After that, the area fell into disrepair due to conflicts during [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]] . According to the Kii Shodo Fudoki, the shrine was revived by [[1443|parishioners]] during the [[Kakitsu]] era ( [[1441|1441-1443]] ). In [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|1585]] [[1585|,]] the shrine's land was confiscated when the Hashiba clan entered the country, but the [[:ja:和歌山城|Wakayama Castle]] lord, [[:ja:桑山重晴|Kuwayama Shigeharu]], restored the shrine buildings. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] considered Sasadahiko Shrine to be important as the guardian deity when he built Wakayama Castle. 神社由緒書。 In 1729, 200 koku of land from Tajiri Village in Nagusa County was donated to [[Kyōhō|him]] . 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 508。 It is also said to be a shrine where people pray for the peace of the nation, and is ordered to perform purification rituals for the peace of the nation 10,000 times a year. 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 247。 From [[Kan'ei|1626]] [[Kanbun (era)|to]] [[1626|1673]] [[1673|,]] Shoshuin served as the temple's betto temple. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, in April [[1873]], it was ranked as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]] under [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system]] . 神社由緒書。 Subsequently, the shrine buildings, treasures, and ancient records were destroyed in fire during the Pacific War. === God Tier === * Junior Fourth Rank Upper ( Kiino Jinmyocho ) - Written as "Sashidahiko-no-kami". Some manuscripts state that he was of Junior Fifth Rank Upper. === Priest === When Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Wakayama Castle, he appointed Okamoto Sasuke, a descendant of the Otomo clan, as its chief priest. 神社由緒書。 In addition, during the restoration by Shigeharu Kuwayama, Iechika Okamoto was designated a priest. Since then, generations of the Okamoto family have served as priests at Sasadahiko Shrine, Okamoto Chojun served as a temporary guardian for Tokugawa Yoshimune, and after Okamoto Chokoku, each generation has had an audience with the shogun once every three years, down to the present day. 神社由緒書。 == Temple grounds == === Shrine === The temple grounds were burned down during the war in 1945, but were later rebuilt. The [[1811]] " [[Bunka|Kiino]] Kuni Meisho Zue" lists Sasadahiko Shrine at the top of its list of famous places, and includes a drawing of the shrine grounds as they were at the time. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_honden-01.JPG|alt=本殿|Main Hall File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_haiden-02.JPG|alt=拝殿|Worship hall === Okanosato Tomb === The ancient tomb is located on the slope of the mountain on the southwest side of the temple grounds and was discovered in January [[1932]] 境内説明板。 . Based on the shape of the pottery excavated, it is estimated to date to around [[6th century|the 6th century]] 『和歌山県史蹟名勝天然記念物調査報告 11輯』（和歌山県、1933年）。, and connections to Sasadahiko Shrine and the Otomo clan have been pointed out . The burial mound is currently buried under falling sand. Only one burial mound has been discovered, but if it is in the form of a group of burial mounds there is a possibility that there are more undiscovered burial mounds. File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|link=File:Sasutahiko-jinja_kofun.JPG|alt=岡の里古墳の位置|location of Okanosato Tomb == Sub-shrines == === Affiliated shrines === [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_Hachiman-sha_&_Hikawa-sha.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|八幡社・氷川社}}]] * Hachiman Shrine - deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]] 摂末社の記載は神社由緒書による。 * Hikawa Shrine - deity: [[Susanoo]] === Sub-shrine === * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Konpira Shrine - deity: Omononushi * Usumisha Shrine - deity: Usumi * Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama-no-Mikoto * Kobayashi Inari Shrine - deity: Ugatama no Mikoto * Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime * Kasuga Shrine - Deities: Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto, Inahinushi-no-Mikoto, Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto, Himegami * Tenmangu Shrine - deity: Sugawara no Michizane * Haraedo Shrine - Deities: Seoritsuhime, Hayaakitsuhime, Ibukito no Kami, Hayasasurahime * Nanryu Hattattsusha Shrine - deity: Nanryu Hattattsu Okami * Daikokusha - deity: Okuninushi * Divine Horse - deity: Lord Aritoku (Tokugawa Yoshimune)'s beloved horse * == deity ==

== Cultural Assets == === Cultural properties destroyed by fire === * Sword with the name Mitsuyo *: [[Tachi|This sword]] is said to have been donated by [[Kyōhō|Tokugawa]] [[Tokugawa Yoshimune|Yoshimune]] in [[1721]] . Mitsuyo was a swordsmith from Miike, Chikugo Province, in the late Kamakura period. The mounting is a thread-wrapped tachi mounting, with all metal fittings made of red copper with a gold-colored diamond pattern on a fish roe background, the scabbard with a gold-colored diamond pattern lacquer-e on a gold pear-colored background, and the handle and waving are brown with a gold border and flower-colored thread winding. The sword box was painted black with wax, had a hinged lid and a lock. 文化庁編『戦災等による焼失文化財 増訂版 美術工芸篇』（臨川書店、1983年）。 In [[Taishō period|1924]] [[1924|,]] it was designated as a former national treasure (equivalent to [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|an important cultural property]] under current law) based on the Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Law of the [[Shōwa period|time]], but was destroyed by fire during the Great Wakayama Air Raid on July 9, [[1945]] . == Festivals == '''location''' * 2-9 Kataokacho [[Wakayama (city)|, Wakayama City,]] Wakayama [[Wakayama Prefecture|Prefecture]] '''Traffic access''' * From Wakayama Station on the West Japan Railway Company (JR West Japan) or Wakayamashi Station on the JR West Japan/ Nankai Electric Railway Company ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Okayamacho" bus stop (approximately 5 minutes walk from the bus stop) ** Take the Wakayama Bus and get off at the "Kencho-mae" bus stop (approximately 7 minutes walk from the bus stop) == Local information == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == footnote == * Shrine History Book * Shikinaisha Research Group (ed.), Shikinaisha Research Report, Kokugakuin University Press, 1977-86 * Junichi Kamada (ed.), "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Jisho," Sengen Jinja, March 10, 1979 * Nozaki Sabun, "Japanese Scenic Places and Geographies, Volume 8: Nankaido Section," Hakubunkan, 1898 * Yoshiyasu Shimizu, Catalog of Famous Places in Japan, Wakayama Prefecture Volume, Taiseikan, 1904 * Edited and published by Wakayama City Hall, "Wakayama History Supplement Edition," Wakayama City Hall, 1915 * " Japanese Historical Place names : Place names in Wakayama Prefecture" ( Heibonsha ) - Wakayama City, Sasadahiko Shrine * Maruyama Kentoku, "Sashidahiko Shrine" (in Kenichi Tanigawa ed., "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 6, Ise, Shima, Iga, Kii" ( Hakusuisha )) * Takao Takaga, "The Otomo Clan: A Famous Warrior Family Descended from the Native Peoples of the Japanese Archipelago (Research on Ancient Clans)," Aogaki Publishing, 2013 * {{ill|Michinoomi-no-mikoto|10=ja|11=道臣命}} *: Ancestor of the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|lt=Ōtomo clan|en}}. According to the Kojiki, he served as the vanguard during {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}} . * {{ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} *: In the "Nihon Shoki" he is written as "Sadehiko." He was the son of {{ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}}, and according to the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}, was the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto. He was sent to the Korean Peninsula and is said to have achieved military success. == External link == {{draft categories| [[Category:coordinates on Wikidata]] [[Category:Pages with unreviewed translations]] [[fr:User:{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Sasihiko Shrine]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Sasadahiko Shrine]] [[Category:File]] [[Category:refreshing the redirects]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Sasadahiko Shrine]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Sasihiko Shrine]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[category{Sasihiko Shrine]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[en:draft: Sasadahiko Shrine]] }}

旧[[県社]]|創建=不詳|本殿=|別名=岡の宮|札所等=|例祭=[[10月17日]]|神事=}} [[File:Sasutahiko-jinja_torii.JPG|right|thumb|200x200px|{{Center|Torii}}]] '''Sasutahiko Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in Kataoka-cho, [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]] [[Wakayama Prefecture|City, Wakayama Prefecture]] . It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. In [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|1585]] [[1585|,]] the shrine's land was confiscated when the Hashiba clan entered the country, but the [[:ja:和歌山城|Wakayama Castle]] lord, [[:ja:桑山重晴|Kuwayama Shigeharu]], restored the shrine buildings. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] considered Sasadahiko Shrine to be important as the guardian deity when he built Wakayama Castle. 神社由緒書。 In 1729, 200 koku of land from Tajiri Village in Nagusa County was donated to [[Kyōhō|him]] . 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 508。 It is also said to be a shrine where people pray for the peace of the nation, and is ordered to perform purification rituals for the peace of the nation 10,000 times a year. 『新訂増補国史大系 45 徳川実紀第8編』吉川弘文館、1970年、p. 247。 From [[Kan'ei|1626]] [[Kanbun (era)|to]] [[1626|1673]] [[1673|,]] Shoshuin served as the temple's betto temple. 『和歌山県の地名』刺田比古神社項。 In [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, in April [[1873]], it was ranked as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]] under [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system]] . 神社由緒書。 Subsequently, the shrine buildings, treasures, and ancient records were destroyed in fire during the Pacific War. === God Tier === * Junior Fourth Rank Upper ( Kiino Jinmyocho ) - Written as "Sashidahiko-no-kami". Some manuscripts state that he was of Junior Fifth Rank Upper. === Priest === When Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Wakayama Castle, he appointed Okamoto Sasuke, a descendant of the Otomo clan, as its chief priest. 神社由緒書。 In addition, during the restoration by Shigeharu Kuwayama, Iechika Okamoto was designated a priest. Since then, generations of the Okamoto family have served as priests at Sasadahiko Shrine, Okamoto Chojun served as a temporary guardian for Tokugawa Yoshimune, and after Okamoto Chokoku, each generation has had an audience with the shogun once every three years, down to the present day. 神社由緒書。 == Temple grounds == === Shrine === The temple grounds were burned down during the war in 1945, but were later rebuilt. The [[1811]] " [[Bunka|Kiino]] Kuni Meisho Zue" lists Sasadahiko Shrine at the top of its list of famous places, and includes a drawing of the shrine grounds as they were at the time. == Cultural Assets == === Cultural properties destroyed by fire === * Sword with the name Mitsuyo *: [[Tachi|This sword]] is said to have been donated by [[Kyōhō|Tokugawa]] [[Tokugawa Yoshimune|Yoshimune]] in [[1721]] . Mitsuyo was a swordsmith from Miike, Chikugo Province, in the late Kamakura period. The mounting is a thread-wrapped tachi mounting, with all metal fittings made of red copper with a gold-colored diamond pattern on a fish roe background, the scabbard with a gold-colored diamond pattern lacquer-e on a gold pear-colored background, and the handle and waving are brown with a gold border and flower-colored thread winding. It is a shrine listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] and [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|its former rank]] was [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|prefectural shrine]] . It is also commonly known as "Oka no Miya" and is also called "Yoshimune Kohitoyoshi Shrine." == Worshipped deities == {{Double image|right|Michinoomi no Mikoto.jpg|110|Otomo no Satehiko.jpg|110|{{Center|[[道臣命]]（左）・[[大伴狭手彦]]（右）}}{{Small|いずれも『[[前賢故実]]』より。道臣命は[[大伴氏]]祖、大伴狭手彦は道臣命十世孫。}}}} [[ja:刺田比古神社]] The two main deities are: 祭神は神社由緒書による。 {{ill|10=ja|11=道臣命|Michiomi no Mikoto}} Founder of the [[:ja:大伴氏|Otomo clan]]. According to the "Kojiki," he served as the vanguard in Emperor {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en}}. {{Ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|en}} Written as "Satehiko" in the "Nihon Shoki." He was the son of {{Ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en}} and is said to be the tenth-generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto according to the "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}." He was dispatched to the Korean Peninsula and achieved military success. === About the deity === Because Sasadahiko Shrine lost ancient documents and treasures during numerous wars, the identity of the ancient deity worshipped at the shrine remains unknown. In the section on shrines in the [[紀伊続風土記|Kii Shoku Fudoki]] (a topographical book of Kii Province from the Edo period), he is identified as {{ill|Sashikuni Okami|lt=Sashikuni Ōkami|ja|刺国大神|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|8=fr}} or [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi]] no Kami, but this is thought to have changed in the Meiji period. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 It is said that the shrine's name has long been known as "Kuzu Myojin," and it appears in the Kan'ei-ki, part of the Kii Shoku Fudoki, on a building inscription from [[1589]] ( [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tensho]] 17), on a stone lantern from [[1650]] ( [[Keian]] 3), and on a building inscription from [[1678]] ( [[Enpō|Enpo]] 6), as "Kunizu Shrine" . For these reasons, there is a view that "Kuzu" is a temporary character for "Kuni no Nushi" and that the deity was originally a landlord. According to the shrine's explanation, when the parishioners rebuilt Sasadahiko Shrine, which had fallen into such ruin that even the enshrined deity was unknown, they named it "Kuninoushi Shrine" with the meaning of "god who protects the country," and this is how the legend that Ōkuninushi is the enshrined deity was born. [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 On the other hand, according to the theory of [[Motoori Norinaga]], Sasadahiko is assumed to be the same as the "Sashikoni-no-Okami" in the Izumo mythology of the Kojiki. 『日本の神々』刺田比古神社項。 According to the Kojiki, {{ill|Sashikuni Ōkami|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni_Okami|fr}} was the father of {{ill|10=ja|11=刺国若比売|Sashikuni Wakahime|en:draft|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Sashikuni Wakahime|}}, who gave birth to Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, and was [[Okuninushi]]'s maternal grandfather. The Kii Shodoki states that Sashikoni Wakahime is named after the place name "Wakaura ( [[:ja:和歌浦|Wakaura]] )," and points out a connection to the fact that Okuninushi came to Kii after being persecuted by the Yatogami. In addition, based on the sound of "sasutahiko," there is a theory that sees Sasutahiko as {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko|en|4=fr|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami}} or Sasutehiko. The only known document that mentions "Sashidahiko" is the "Furuya Family Genealogy" included in the "Kaino Kuni Ichinomiya Sengen Jinja Shiho" 『甲斐国一之宮浅間神社誌』浅間神社、1979年、資料篇のpp. 278-300所収。古屋家は[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]の社家。 . The "Furuya Family Genealogy" states that Michiomi’s father was Sasadahiko, and that Michiomi was “born in Kataoka, Nagusa County, Kii Province.” [https://okanomiya.com/yurai/ 刺田比古の由来]（神社公式サイト内）。 Based on this record, the Sasadahiko Shrine has speculated that Sasadahiko was originally enshrined as an ancestral deity. The Furuya Family Genealogy was first published in 1979 and is therefore not widely known, but it is highly regarded by researchers. [[:ja:田中卓|Taku Tanaka]] has stated that "in fact, there are many points in the existing Otomo family tree that have been corrected or added to by this genealogy" 『田中卓著作集 6』国書刊行会　1986年、p. 160。, and Mutsuko Mizoguchi has also evaluated it as "an extremely valuable document that has retained the original form" 『古代氏族の系譜』吉川弘文館、1987年、p. 96。同著で溝口は「古屋家家譜」を詳細に分析している。 . The traditional genealogy of the Otomo clan is known as the "Otomo clan genealogy" 「大伴氏系図」『[[続群書類従]]』巻第182所収。 published in the " [[:ja:群書類従|Zoku Gunsho Ruiju]] ," but it contains many errors, such as listing [[:ja:大伴長徳|Otomo Naganori]] 's son as [[:ja:大伴古麻呂|Furumaro]], and in recent years, many have adopted the "Furuya family genealogy" [[宝賀寿男]]『古代氏族系譜集成』（古代氏族研究会、1986年）も『古屋家家譜』の内容を採用する。 . == history == === consecration_year === According to the shrine's tradition, Otomo no Sakehiko, the tenth generation descendant of Michiomi no Mikoto, was bestowed with the local area, "Oka no Sato," as a reward for his achievements, and the area continued to be ruled by successive generations after him. 神社由緒書。 Later, when his twentieth-generation [[:ja:大伴武以|descendant, Otomo no Takemochi]], came to live in the area, he enshrined his ancestral deity here, which is said to be the founding of the shrine. The local people worshiped him as "Kuni no Nushi no Kami" or "Okuninushi no Kami" . The Sasadahiko Shrine side considers the "Oka no Sato Kofun" ancient tomb within the shrine grounds to be the grave of the Otomo clan, and also points out the deep ties between this area and the Otomo clan based on the description of the Otomo clan from "Kataoka Village, Nagusa County" in Volume 30 of the " [[Shoku Nihongi]] " 『続日本紀』神護景雲3年（769年）11月25日条。 . 神社由緒書。 === Brief history === In [[Enchō|the Engishiki]] [[Engishiki|Shinmeicho]] ( [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|list of]] shrines) compiled in 927, the shrine is listed as "Sashidahiko Shrine" in [[Kii Province|Nagusa County, Kii]] [[:ja:名草郡|Province]], and is listed as one of the shrines listed in [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|the Engishiki]] .
